page: Amazon Web Services t3a.large is an entry-level burstable instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. It is equipped with an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7571 processor running at 2.2 GHz, providing 2 vCPUs backed by 1 physical core and 2 threads per core. System memory is configured with 8.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, reflecting a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation. The instance includes no bundled local storage, relying on network-attached storage solutions, and provides a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps without dedicated GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks place the t3a.large in the entry tier for compute and memory throughput. It achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 683.0 and a multi-core score of 923.0, along with a PassMark CPU score of 1856.65 and a stress-ng multi-core result of 588.49. Uncached memory read bandwidth measured 20.46 GB/s, while write bandwidth reached 11.52 GB/s. In application benchmarks, the instance delivered 1.21 million operations per second on Redis SET tests and 1.48 GB/s in static web serving. Support for AES and SHA-NI cryptographic extensions contributed to stronger relative performance in encryption tests compared to general floating-point and vector workloads.

From an infrastructure and operational perspective, the burstable CPU allocation allows resource density and cost efficiency for workloads that do not maintain continuous high CPU utilization. The primary tradeoff is constrained sustained compute and absence of local high-speed disk arrays. The configuration is appropriate for low-traffic web applications, staging and development environments, lightweight background workers, and low-volume microservices.
description: Amazon Web Services t3a.large is a burstable general-purpose virtual instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It is configured with 2 vCPUs from a single physical core on a 2.2 GHz AMD EPYC 7571 processor, complemented by 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory. The instance features no bundled local storage, operating with remote network-attached disks and a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and does not include GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations place the instance in the lower tier for sustained raw processing, registering 683.0 in Geekbench single-core testing and 1.21 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks. The burstable CPU model makes it an efficient option for non-continuous computational demand. It is appropriate for lightweight web serving, development servers, simple microservices, and low-intensity background tasks.
